chief_complaint: Stage 2 hypertension with associated metabolic risk factors (obesity, prediabetes) and chronic sinusitis
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 43-year-old male with a long-standing history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 1995, currently uncontrolled (BP 149/91 mmHg). Obesity (BMI >=30) was documented in 2017 and persists. Prediabetes was identified in 2014 (A1c 6.3%). Anemia has been present since 2015 without a documented work‑up. He has chronic sinusitis noted in 2018 and a prior episode of acute bacterial sinusitis in 2017. Ongoing psychosocial stress and exposure to violence in his environment have been recorded since 2017. He is employed full‑time and has completed higher education. The medication regimen is limited to low‑dose losartan and diphenhydramine, suggesting suboptimal management of his hypertension and sinus symptoms.

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include gingivitis (resolved 2017-08-15) and prior medication review reminders (resolved 2016-07-25 and 2017-07-31). The patient previously held part‑time employment (resolved 2017-07-31) and an earlier period of full‑time employment (resolved 2016-07-25).
social_determinants: Employed full‑time; reports exposure to violence in his environment; experiences chronic stress; has completed higher education; no documented smoking, alcohol, or substance use information.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure is in stage 2 hypertension (SBP 149, DBP 91). Obesity is present (BMI >=30) though exact value is missing. Glycemic control is prediabetic (A1c 6.3%). Anemia of unspecified type is documented. No lipid panel, eGFR, or renal labs are available, limiting assessment of cardiovascular and renal risk. Comorbidity flags indicate hypertension and anemia. Overall organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes), renal (potential CKD risk), metabolic (progression to diabetes), hematologic (anemia), ENT (chronic sinusitis), and mental health (stress, environmental violence).
